back: A verb + particle (adverb or preposition) that together have their own meaning.
notes: give up, look after, put up with

back: A pronoun goes between the verb and the particle: turn it off, pick them up, call it off.
break down (stop working), break into (enter by force), break out (start suddenly), break up (end a relationship).
call off = cancel; put off = postpone; carry out = conduct; look into = investigate.
turn down = reject; set up = establish; find out = discover; put up with = tolerate; go on = continue.
look after (care for), look into (investigate), look up to (admire), look for (search for), look forward to (anticipate with pleasure).
A noun or an -ing form: I look forward to hearing from you.
take after (resemble), take off (leave the ground; remove; become successful), take over (gain control), take up (start a hobby).
fill in (or out) a form; fill up a container or tank.
